introduction.heading: What is React?
introduction.description: React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces with reusable components. It makes creating interactive UIs painless by managing component state and rendering efficiently.

hooks.heading: React Hooks
hooks.description: Hooks let you use state and other React features in function components. Common hooks include useState, useEffect, useContext, and useReducer.

practiceTopics.title: Components & JSX
practiceTopics.description: Learn to create and render components

fullExample.heading: Full Example, Step by Step
fullExample.title: A small React app: state, props, and an effect
fullExample.description: This example ties together the core concepts above in one realistic component. Click through the steps to see which lines each one is talking about.
code: // A small presentational component - it only reads the "name" prop,
// useState gives this component its own piece of memory that
// useEffect runs after React commits this render to the screen.
// Because count is in the dependency array, it only re-runs

steps.label: Import the hooks you need
steps.explanation: useState and useEffect are named exports from the "react" package. You only import the hooks a file actually uses.

steps.label: Build a presentational component
steps.explanation: Greeting is just a function that returns JSX. It receives name as a prop and renders it - it has no state of its own, so the same input always produces the same output.

steps.label: Create state with useState
steps.explanation: useState(initialValue) returns a [value, setter] pair. Calling the setter (setName, setCount) tells React this component's data changed and schedules a re-render with the new value.

steps.label: Run side effects with useEffect
steps.explanation: The function passed to useEffect runs after React updates the screen. The dependency array [count] tells React to only re-run it when count changes, instead of after every render.

steps.label: Pass data down as props
steps.explanation: The input's value and onChange are wired to the name state, and that same name is passed into <Greeting name={name} /> as a prop - data flows down from parent to child.

steps.label: Handle events and update state
steps.explanation: onClick is a plain event handler. Calling setCount(count + 1) updates state, which makes App - and anything reading count - re-render with the new value.

steps.label: Export the component
steps.explanation: export default makes App importable from other files, e.g. by the file that mounts it into the page with ReactDOM.createRoot(...).render(<App />).
